src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: `parseState` checks against the domain's `orderStates` instead of a local copy of the states
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only `createApp()` and `app.listen(...)`, so it is just the entry point
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: `createApp(service = new OrderService(new InMemoryFulfilmentStore()))` wires the store into the service through the port
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files form one cohesive infrastructure boundary: http-app.ts is the HTTP adapter (createApp), in-memory-store.ts implements the application's FulfilmentStore port (InMemoryFulfilmentStore), and server.ts is the entry point that calls createApp(). The routes go only through OrderService and never touch the store directly. The store is used only via the port it implements. http-app.ts only checks the shape of incoming values (stringField, numberField, parseItems, parseState). parseState checks against the domain's own orderStates list rather than a copied one, so no domain rule is duplicated. Minor issues outside this rule: request-parsing errors are thrown as DomainError, so they return 409 instead of 400, and server.ts logs the raw parsed port even when it falls back to 3000. Neither splits the module's concern, duplicates a rule or bypasses the module's abstractions.
